prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1145; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is for claim file purposes. Do you understand and consent to being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state the location where the accident occurred.

A: It was at an intersection in Conroe, Texas. I was heading through on the main road when another vehicle came in from the side street.

Q: Can you describe the traffic signals at that intersection at the time?

A: My light was green. I'm pretty sure of that because I had just cleared the previous block and I was watching the signal turn.

Q: What happened next?

A: The other car didn't stop. It came out from the cross street and hit the driver's side of my vehicle. I tried to brake but there wasn't enough time.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I didn't hit my head. I was shaken up, but I stayed conscious the whole time.

Q: Where do you feel injuries?

A: My right shoulder mainly. It hurts when I raise my arm above my head, and I've got some stiffness in my neck too.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same day and they took X-rays. I've scheduled a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist.

Q: Did anyone else witness the collision?

A: I think a pedestrian stopped to help. I didn't get their information, but there may have been a witness at the gas station on the corner.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want my vehicle looked at properly, and I'd appreciate it if the claim could move along since I'm not able to work full duty right now.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
